title: Cluster feeding: normal or starving?
summary: Frequent feeds in a short window are common, especially in the first weeks.
whatsNormal:
Cluster feeding means your baby wants many feeds close together, often in the evening or before a longer sleep stretch.

• Common around growth spurts (often days 2–3, 2–3 weeks, 6 weeks)
• Baby may feed every 30–60 minutes for a few hours
• Hands to mouth, rooting, and short naps between feeds are typical
• After cluster feeding, many babies take a longer sleep period

This pattern does not usually mean your milk is gone. It often helps bring milk in and builds supply with breastfeeding.
watchFor: Fewer than expected wet diapers after day 4 (see wet diaper guide)
Baby cannot be comforted between feeds and cries continuously for hours
Very sleepy baby who will not wake for feeds every 2–3 hours in the first weeks
Signs of dehydration: sunken soft spot, dry mouth, no wet diapers
callDoctorIf: No wet diapers for 12+ hours after day 3
Weight loss beyond what your pediatrician discussed at the first visit
Fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher if under 3 months
You are worried about feeding or weight, call; lactation support can help too
